knowledge_point.title: Reducing an Augmented Matrix for a Singular 2x2 System to REF and Solving the Resulting System

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 9 & 24 \\ 4 & 12 & 32 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 9 & 24 \\ 4 & 12 & 32 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 4 & 12 & 32 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The system corresponding to $M$ is 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=9\\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-2y=9.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2y+9,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2y+9\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\  y \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 2y+9 \\  y \end{bmatrix}=⟨2y+9,y⟩,\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
